_about: Gen9 / Gen9.5 GT2 facts for models and solvers (docs/solvers.md section 4). Every value has a tag (SPEC = documentation, MEAS = measured here, SW = driver/compiler behaviour, EST = Mesa heuristic, HYP = unconfirmed) and a source. Unknowns are listed explicitly; a model that depends on one must say so. Keep in sync with docs/performance-model.md (the source of truth for prose).

uhd620.name: UHD 620 (Whiskey Lake, Gen9.5 GT2)
uhd620.ram: 2 x DDR4-2400 (dual channel) / 1 x DDR4-2400 (single channel)

hd530.name: HD 530 (Skylake, Gen9 GT2)
hd530.note: same ISA and binary code as whl (results/attn-kcl-hd530-2026-11-13.txt)

grf.per: hardware thread (fixed; does not trade against thread count)
grf.reserved_note: r0 thread payload; asm/gemm_gen.free_regs also keeps r1 and r127

occupancy_tradeoff.value: none assumed: 7 threads per EU regardless of registers
occupancy_tradeoff.note: to verify; NVIDIA/AMD-style register-vs-occupancy trade-offs do not apply in this form

banks.rule: mad src1 and src2 in the same bank conflict; src0 does not matter

conflicts_with.igc_comment: src1/src2 collision 'upto pre-SKL' (visa/GraphColor.cpp); whether hasBankCollision() is true on SKL: unknown

unknown: measured on UHD 620 only (repeat on HD 530)

notes: FP16 mad needs -cl-fast-relaxed-math (else mul+add, 200 vs 791 GFLOPS) [MEAS]
FP16 two-operand ops with a scalar operand lose the double rate [MEAS]
SIMD16 not allowed for packed-f16 results of mixed mode [SW]

issue.model: in-order per thread; threads of an EU interleave
issue.observed: attention loop 1229 instructions / 1024 mad: 0.90-0.92 of the issue bound; OA stall 2-3 % (latency hidden by other threads)
issue.observed_source: results/attn-asm-hd530-2026-11-13.txt; message from the attention session 2026-11-13

memory.page_note: tiles touching many distant rows collapse 15-20x (TLB) [MEAS, docs/pitfalls.md section 2]

l3_port_ceiling.note: OWord block reads, >= 2 in flight per thread; same for work-group 64/128 and a 1 MB region; up to 12 SIMD8 FP32 mads per 128 B hide under the reads. Qwen attention (16 mads per block) is issue-bound at ~88 % of this ceiling, not port-bound. OA L3ShaderThroughput matches true bytes once scaled by the OA clock (97-100 %).

sampler_read.note: sample_ld SIMD8 RGBA32: the sampler adds at most ~20 % to the data port for L3-resident data; beyond L3 mixing is slower than the port alone

send.header_rule: the send reads its header at issue: one header can be advanced right after each send and shared

model_effective.source: results/mt-model-2026-11-13.txt (fitted on 3 Qwen points, checked on 2 Llama points within 3 %)
model_effective.note: effective values of the multithreaded model, not hardware constants; port_bytes_per_clk_per_eu 6 is below the measured port ceiling (7.1-7.6, memory.l3_port_ceiling): in the model it stands for issue overhead and latency effects, not the data port alone
